nodes.body:
**Question**

Is there a case in which we would expect to be stripping query params in the real world? I ask because the original issue was about cloning from in the file tree, which should just be extra path entries.

I was just a bit extra defensive on this and wanted to cover cases where one might copy a PR link (e.g., a link to a comment) or a deep-link to a line in a file. In these cases, there'll be a fragment at the end of the URL. I can't imagine what kind of links could come with a query parameter, but again decided to strip them away to be safe.

I agree this is so niche and could never happen in reality. If you think there's no value in that, I can update the PR.

It's probably more complicated to not do it. We'd have to error out if someone provided a URL with a query string. I think the main issue is that when I read code I **really** want to know what user flow it is supporting. I think the best thing to do would be to expand on your `simplifyURL` comment to include when this is important e.g. if the user copies and pastes from the file tree browser or from a comment URL.
